fields.description:
## Context / Problem
`_pai_structured` manually creates fresh Agent runs for prompted-output recovery, so output attempts can reset the request budget and retry history is assembled outside Pydantic (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:87-178`). The approved RP-01 contract instead uses the Pydantic output-policy adapter [rebar:grazeable-preferred-bumblebee] (S1, now landed: `src/rebar/llm/pai_output.py` — review against `--ref HEAD`, which carries the stacked S1 change) in one Agent operation while preserving every authoritative input and stored response.

## Approach
Replace the manual structured-output attempt scheduler with one Pydantic `Agent` run that composes the S1 adapter (`pai_output.output_function` as `output_type=TextOutput(fn)`) with two new seams from a focused `src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py` helper:

1. **Wire-context projection — a pydantic-ai `history_processors` `HistoryProcessor`.** The concrete seam is the Agent-level `history_processors=[proc]` (`pydantic_ai._history_processor.HistoryProcessor`): a callable run before each model request that returns a COPY for the wire without mutating stored state, so `result.all_messages()` keeps the full history regardless of what the wire copy omits. It includes the complete failed `ModelResponse` on the retry wire ONLY when every viable candidate has a known window and a token count proving `input_tokens + effective_max_tokens <= window`; otherwise it omits that response WHOLE (never partially). Unknown window/count → omit. Authoritative input (system/user/tool) that cannot fit fails closed with a typed fit/context error — never shortened.

2. **Truncation reclassification — a concision-aware operation guard.** For this operation ONLY, `pai_retry` supplies its own `after_model_request` capability (attached INSTEAD OF `pai_output.guard_capability()`, whose terminal-truncation contract stays UNCHANGED for every other caller (until S5 cutover). This guard co-locates the reclassification: (a) on `finish_reason` `length`/`max_tokens`, before parsing, raises `pydantic_ai.ModelRetry("Make your response as concise as possible while fulfilling the prompt and output format requirements.")` — a bounded, in-run retry; (b) otherwise delegates to `structured.check_response(response)`, so refusal/`content_filter` raise the terminal `UnretryableOutputError` (one call, no retry) and a transient `error` raises the retryable `StructuredOutputError`. The shared `structured.py` classification tables (`_UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS`, `check_stop_reason`) are NOT modified.

3. **One shared request budget, one shared retry counter.** `structured_run.py`'s `build_usage_limits` sets the operation-wide `UsageLimits.request_limit` = base request allowance (`ceil(eff_max_iter/2)`) PLUS the configured output-retry allowance, computed once with NO per-attempt reset. Crucially the value it RETURNS as `req_limit` (consumed by telemetry and by `completion_banking.iteration_limit_for`) stays the BARE base `ceil(eff_max_iter/2)`; the output allowance is an addend only inside the constructed `UsageLimits`, so the `iteration_limit = 2×B` inverse is preserved exactly. Output-size (concision) retries and parse/validation retries draw from the SAME counter — the configured output-retry allowance `structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES` (=2), lowered only by `req.structured_retry_limit` — not a separate budget. A single truncation spends one unit; repeated output-size failure exhausts it and surfaces the typed exhaustion error.

The concision reclassification is an in-run `ModelRetry`, so it never raises a model exception and never reaches the `FallbackModel` `fallback_on` predicate — output-size retry structurally cannot trigger fallback.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/pai_retry.py` — new: (a) the `HistoryProcessor` wire-context projection (fit decision + non-mutating whole-response include/omit) and (b) the concision-aware operation guard (`length`/`max_tokens` → bounded concision `ModelRetry`; delegate refusal/`content_filter`/`error` to `structured.check_response`). A module docstring records the combined-allowance derivation and that it is raiseable via a normal reviewed follow-up if recovery is starved. No provider selection, usage projection, or persistence.
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — replace the manual `_pai_structured` attempt scheduling with one Agent operation; extend `build_usage_limits` to derive the combined operation-wide `request_limit` (base + output allowance) without resetting counters (this is where `req_limit` is computed, not `agent_call.py`).
- `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py` — thread the derived output-retry allowance and the two new seams into the built Agent kwargs (`retries={"output": allowance}`, `capabilities=[concision_guard]`, `history_processors=[wire_projection]`); it holds `build_agent_kwargs`, and gains only this wiring — it does not compute the allowance.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — compose the helper at the call site without growing past the 800-line cap.
- `tests/unit/test_structured_run.py`, `tests/unit/test_runner_pydantic_budget.py`, `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` — operation, history, and limit contracts.

**Cross-directory consumers of the `ceil(eff_max_iter/2)` formula.** The one control-flow consumer is `workflow/completion_banking.py:iteration_limit_for`, which inverts it as `iteration_limit = 2×B`; `usage_log.py`/`runner.py` merely receive the already-built `request_limit`/`req_limit` as arguments. Because `build_usage_limits` keeps RETURNING the bare base `req_limit` (the allowance lives only inside the constructed `UsageLimits`), `iteration_limit_for` stays exact and is intentionally unaffected — the output reserve is a bounded per-run recovery addend, not banked successor-pool capacity. A source-census test asserts the returned `req_limit` still equals `ceil(eff_max_iter/2)` while `UsageLimits.request_limit` equals base+allowance, and that no other module encodes the bare formula.

## Testing
- Happy: invalid-then-valid succeeds in two Agent requests, one operation result, one shared `UsageLimits`.
- Boundary: complete response fits (on wire) / does not fit (omitted whole, `all_messages()` complete) / count unknown (omitted) / authoritative input cannot fit (typed error, no shortening).
- Limit: tool turn + output retry succeeds at the derived allowance and fails one below it; repeated output-size failure exhausts the shared allowance.
- Terminal: refusal/content-filter is one call, no output retry, no fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Invalid-then-valid structured output completes through one Pydantic Agent run and reports exactly two Pydantic requests under one shared `UsageLimits`; verified by focused real-`FunctionModel` tests.
- [ ] A complete 5,000-character failed response is present on the retry wire only when the full request plus output reserve provably fits (`input_tokens + effective_max_tokens <= window` for every viable candidate); verified by a complete-fit test.
- [ ] When it does not fit — or window/token count is unknown — zero characters from that response are on the retry wire, while `result.all_messages()` retains all 5,000; verified by omit and unknown-count tests.
- [ ] Authoritative-input overflow raises the typed fit/context failure without shortening system, user, or tool content; verified by an oversize-input failure test.
- [ ] `length`/`max_tokens` consumes at most the configured output-retry allowance (shared with parse/validation retries; not a separate counter) and sends exactly "Make your response as concise as possible while fulfilling the prompt and output format requirements."; verified by a success case and an exhaustion case.
- [ ] Refusal/content-filter remains terminal after one model call and activates neither output retry nor provider fallback (structurally: an in-run `ModelRetry` never reaches the `fallback_on` predicate); verified by call-count and candidate-count assertions.
- [ ] The combined request allowance is documented in the `pai_retry.py` module docstring as raiseable through a normal reviewed follow-up, and no per-attempt reset path remains in the new scheduler; verified by that docstring plus a source-census and budget test.
